title: One clock, two noons
hook: Madrid and Barcelona show the same time. Do they get noon together?

knows: that Madrid and Barcelona share one clock time
that the Sun is highest around midday
doesNotKnow: that the Sun's peak arrives earlier further east
how much earlier per degree of longitude

misconception: Two cities on the same official clock reach midday at the same moment.
objective: The learner can say that solar noon moves 4 minutes per degree of longitude, so Barcelona's sun peaks about 23 minutes before Madrid's.

claims.text: Barcelona is about 505 km east of Madrid, 5.9 degrees of longitude apart.
claims.source: Builder's node check: great-circle Madrid (40.4168 N, 3.7038 W) to Barcelona (41.3874 N, 2.1686 E) = 505.1 km on R = 6,371.0088 km; longitude difference 5.8724 degrees. City coordinates from memory (gazetteer values), not re-checked. 'East' is nearly due east; Barcelona is also about 1 degree further north.

claims.text: The Sun's highest point moves 4 minutes per degree of longitude: 360 degrees in 24 hours.
claims.source: 24 h x 60 / 360 = 4 min per degree. Any astronomy text; mean solar time.

claims.text: The Sun reaches its highest point in Barcelona about 23 minutes (23.5) before Madrid.
claims.source: 5.8724 x 4 = 23.49 min. The equation of time shifts both cities by the same amount, so the difference holds (brief's reasoning). The stage computes the same figure from the two longitudes; the line sits at Barcelona's longitude at 0 min and at Madrid's at 23.5 min.

claims.text: Madrid and Barcelona keep the same official clock.
claims.source: From memory, not re-checked: mainland Spain uses one time zone (CET/CEST). No claim is made about why.

claims.text: The Sun moves west across the sky, so the peak reaches the west later.
claims.source: Earth turns west to east, so the noon line travels east to west. The stage draws it moving west.

claims.text: The stage map is equirectangular, so east-west distances on it are stretched compared with north-south ones at this latitude.
claims.source: Snyder (1987): equirectangular uses the same scale on both axes in degrees; at 40 N a degree of longitude is about 0.77 of a degree of latitude (cos 40). Only the label 'Equirectangular map' is shown on the stage.

recall.question: Two places 5 degrees of longitude apart on one clock: by how much do their solar noons differ?
recall.why: The Sun's peak moves 4 minutes per degree of longitude, so 5 degrees is 20 minutes.
